description:
## Why this issue exists

stoa-tls and stoa-mail do not explicitly configure a minimum TLS version or an approved cipher suite list. The default from rustls or the OS may allow TLS 1.0/1.1 or weak ciphers depending on library version. PCI-DSS 4.2.1 requires TLS 1.2 minimum; SOC2 CC6.7 requires encrypted transport with industry-standard configurations.

## What needs to be done

- In stoa-tls, set minimum protocol version to TLS 1.2 explicitly via rustls `ServerConfig` / `ClientConfig`.
- Define an approved cipher suite list: at minimum `TLS13_AES_256_GCM_SHA384`, `TLS13_AES_128_GCM_SHA256`, `TLS13_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256`, and the TLS 1.2 ECDHE-ECDSA/RSA AES-GCM suites.
- Expose these as config keys with a documented default that satisfies PCI-DSS.
- Add a startup log line that prints the effective min TLS version and cipher suite count.
- Add a test that attempts a TLS 1.1 connection and verifies rejection.

## Acceptance criteria

- TLS 1.1 and below connections are rejected
- Cipher suite list matches the PCI-DSS 4.2.1 approved list
- Config keys documented with regulatory defaults
- Startup log shows effective TLS policy

## Design notes

Regulatory refs: PCI-DSS 4.2.1, SOC2 CC6.7. rustls enforces TLS 1.2+ by default in recent versions — this epic is about making the enforcement explicit and testable, not relying on library defaults.
notes: Implementation verified via single-bash-call test run (all 10 stoa-tls tests pass, all 5 reader starttls tests pass, fmt+clippy clean). Files need to be applied to the real git working tree. The verified file content was written in bash test runs but the opencode Write tool writes appear to not persist to the actual filesystem in this environment. User should apply changes manually or re-run the implementation script.
title: Explicit TLS policy: minimum version and cipher suites
